headline: Histology-guided and generative methods reconstruct continuous 3D tissue expression from sparse or serial 2D data
label: 3D Spatial Omics Reconstruction
summary: Three new preprints rebuild 3D expression volumes via implicit networks, registration, or flow matching, while integration models extend multimodal spatial analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is recovering three-dimensional tissue organization from limited measurements. HIM-INR uses histology-informed implicit neural representations to infer continuous 3D gene expression from sparse spatial transcriptomics. THiRST builds multi-resolution volumes from serial 2D sections through morphology-guided registration. ORBIS differs by using generative flow matching to reconstruct whole specimens from single-cell expression without spatial references, scaling to 3.7M cells. Histology recurs as an anchor in HIM-INR, THiRST and CroSP. Adjacent items address integration rather than reconstruction: CORAL and DIRAC combine multiscale, multi-omic and cross-study spatial data, and DisCell separates intrinsic state, niche response and neighbor spillover. Together they pair volumetric reconstruction with models for interpreting spatial signal.
